INTERNSHIP SPOTLIGHT
Ivan Vashchenko
MECHANICAL ENGINEERING INTERN
WTI SERVICES PURE AIR | CLEARWATER, FL
Sophomore Ivan Vashchenko finished up his first
year of classes at Principia and then headed to
Clearwater, FL for a summer internship with WTI
Services Pure Air working in their Engineering/
Estimating department. Ivan found this position
online through ZipRecruiter. This internship also
resulted in a full-year remote Intern position for Ivan.
WTI Services Pure Air, provides consulting, evaluation
and engineered services to improve the HVAC system
performance, occupant comfort and energy efficiency
of its clients’ facilities.
WTI’s Engineering/Estimating department is
responsible for all necessary engineering work. They
estimate the scope of work by analyzing the current
condition of an air handling unit. The design team
creates drawings that show how everything should
look once a job is complete. This department also
writes proposals and reports for clients.
Ivan contributed to the team both as a full-stack
developer -- helping create estimation automation
tools, and as a Mechanical Engineer -- conducting
site visits, assessing units, and creating drawings.
Through this experience, Ivan learned a lot
about HVAC, including how Air Handler Unit
(AHU) restoration works, the details of each AHU
component, and design aspects. More importantly
he learned about working in the corporate world and
understanding the needed skills that set engineers up
for success.
Classes at Principia prepared him for this internship.
First, his classes created an environment where he
learned how to think outside of the box. Additionally,
by taking numerous physics, calculus, and chemistry
classes, he developed strong problem-solving skills
and the ability to adapt quickly. HVAC industry
knowledge has been beneficial to this semester’s
Fluid Mechanics class.
Since this was Ivan’s first internship immediately
following his freshman year, he plans to explore
different engineering fields. He is particularly
interested in Autopilot and Autonomous Driving
technologies, but he can also see himself continuing
work in areas related to heat exchange.
His internship advice to his fellow engineering friends
is not to hesitate to apply for an internship, even if
the work description sounds more advanced than
your current skills. Always connect with as many
people as you can. Start researching companies you
are interested in right now. Seek as much outside the
classroom experience as possible; on-campus jobs,
clubs, individual and group projects.
